"handy, dexterous, having special manual ability," apparently from East Anglian dialectal… See origin and meaning of clever. from East Anglian dialectal cliver "expert at seizing," perhaps from East Frisian klüfer "skillful," or Norwegian dialectic klover "ready, skillful," and perhaps influenced by Old English clifer "claw, hand" (early usages seem to refer to dexterity).
